name: Example Quickling Apps Co (fictional)
summary: A fictional app maker growing revenue about 50% a year. Margins are thin, free cash flow is negative, and growth is partly paid for with new debt. The share price is high compared with its earnings.
assumptions: All figures are fictional and in millions of USD, except the share price. The same tax rate (25% of pre-tax profit), tax rules and accounting apply to every company. No one-off items, share issues or buybacks. Ratios use Year 3 and the current share price. Simulated for learning; not a real firm.
notes: Fast revenue growth, but operating expenses grew even faster in Year 3 (+56% vs +50%), so the operating margin slipped from 10% to under 9%.
Spending on equipment and software (capital expenditure) is bigger than the cash the business brings in, so free cash flow is negative and debt has doubled in two years.
The high P/E means buyers are paying today for profits the company has not made yet. If growth slows, the price has a long way to fall even if the business is fine.
Competitive position unclear: other fictional app makers could copy its product, and customers may switch easily.
